title: Insurance Claim Services Controller Policy on Receivable Write-Offs
content:
**Policy.** The claim file must be in approved status when a write-off is posted. A write-off names the approval line it reduces and never exceeds that line's amount less earlier write-offs of it. Program price adjustment applies only on Carrier Program Claim Billing, where the carrier's program pricing review is final and the difference is never billed to the insured. Carrier denied line records a line the carrier declined after approval; on tiers where denied lines are billable to the customer, the same amount stays owed by the customer on the job, and on Assignment of Benefits and Carrier Program files it is never billed to the customer. A carrier denied line write-off larger than the tier's desk write-off cap is not posted by the desk. A larger write-off, or a remaining dispute at or above the tier's appraisal referral threshold, is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy. Depreciation forfeited is posted only after the depreciation window has passed without a request.

This Insurance Claim Services policy governs every write-off posted against a carrier approval line. The desk cap, the appraisal referral threshold and whether denied lines are billable are each tier's own figures.

## Retired clauses

- The clause "carrier denied line records a line the carrier declined after approval;" is no longer in force as written here; it has been superseded by the current Insurance Claim Services basis.
- The clause "on tiers where denied lines are billable to the customer, the same amount stays owed by the customer on the job," is no longer in force as written here; it has been superseded by the current Insurance Claim Services basis.
- The words "and on Assignment of Benefits and Carrier Program files it is never billed to the customer" remain in force, as does every other sentence of the policy.

## Reasons

| Write-off reason | Where and when it applies |
|---|---|
| program price adjustment | only on Carrier Program Claim Billing; the difference is never billed to the insured |
| carrier denied line | never billed to the customer on Assignment of Benefits and Carrier Program files |
| depreciation forfeited | only after the depreciation window has passed without a request |

## Limits

- Evidence: the claim file's status (approved) and the approval line named, with its amount and earlier write-offs, on the system record.
- Line limit (hypothetical): an approval line of 1200.00 already reduced by 300.00 can take a further write-off of at most 900.00.
- Desk cap (hypothetical cap of 750.00): a carrier denied line write-off of 750.00 may be posted by the desk; one of 750.01 is not, and is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.
- A remaining dispute at or above the tier's appraisal referral threshold is likewise handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.
